x: Explain the importance of ijma to Shari'ah Law.
n: Candidates who understood ijma developed it into Level 2–3, linking it to Shari'ah and the modern world; some wrote only about Shari'ah and dropped marks.

x: Assess the view that only the choices a person makes affect their final judgement. (Hadith on al-Qadr)
Identify two categories of Ahkam pentad.
n: The most poorly answered (a) on the paper: many candidates did not know the five categories.

x: Explain the importance of manners for Muslims as outlined in the Qur'an.
n: The best answers showed how good manners present the Islamic faith in the best light, with examples.

x: Assess the view that Ibrahim was the most important prophet before Muhammad (pbuh). (Qur'an 9:128-129)
Give one condition for the declaration of lesser jihad.
Describe how the Shahadah is used in Muslim daily practice.
n: Most gained a mark by linking the Shahadah to daily prayer and developed it with the Ummah uniting in prayer; good answers also linked it to birth and conversion.

x: Explain Muslim teachings on the purpose of families.
n: Well answered: many reached Level 2; Level 3 needed accurate facts and a broad range of fully developed themes.

x: Assess the view that the main purpose of Salah is to unite all Muslims. (Qur'an 62:9-11)
n: Level 3 answers used 62:9-11 and Jumu'ah for unity, then a deeper relationship with Allah as the other view.

x: Identify one Islamic festival observed by all Muslims.
Describe how some Muslims give Khums.
n: Well answered by candidates who knew the difference between Khums and Zakah; most gained marks from its use to help those in need.

x: Explain why the Prophet and his successors are good examples of leadership for Muslims.
n: Many used the Prophet's character as a guide for leadership today (at least Level 2); better answers also used successors such as Abu Bakr and Uthman (Level 3).

x: Assess the view that Hajj must be performed by all Muslims. (Qur'an 2:197-199)
n: Strong answers used the text, then an alternative view such as not being able to go because of financial difficulty or illness.

x: Identify two problems the Prophet and his followers faced in Makkah before the Hijrah.
Describe the Prophet's relationship with people of other religions.
Explain the importance of the Prophet's relationship with his wives and children.
'Without the events of the Hijrah, Islam would not have succeeded in spreading the message of Allah.' Assess this statement. (Hadith on intentions)
Identify two ways Ali Ibn Talib supported Muhammad (pbuh).
Describe the events of the battle of Khyber.
Explain Muslim beliefs about the nature of society.
'The Night of Power is the most important event in Islam.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 97:1-5)
Identify two roles performed by the angel Mikail.
Describe the role of Isma'il as a prophet in Islam.
Explain the importance of qiyas to Shari'ah Law.
n: The best answers explained qiyas as judging new practices by analogy with earlier rulings; writing only about Shari'ah dropped marks.

x: 'Being merciful and just are the most important attributes of Allah.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 112:1-4)
Identify two acts considered mandub (recommended).
Describe what the Injil teaches according to the Qur'an.
Explain the importance of belief in predestination for Muslims.
'Belief in Akhirah is what motivates Muslims to live good lives.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 101:1-11)
Give one reason Muslims give to charity.
Describe how Muslims perform Salah.
n: Most gained full marks by saying what Salah is, then describing the prayer movements and the direction of prayer.

x: Explain the importance of the greater (inner) jihad in the life of Muslims.
n: Best answers covered the nafs, spirituality, society and closeness to Allah; describing lesser jihad lost marks.

x: 'Marriage and procreation are the most important ways of strengthening the Ummah.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 30:21)
n: Strong answers used 30:21, then other ways of strengthening the Ummah, such as imams teaching in mosques.

x: Give one feature of Hajj.
Describe the challenges faced by Islamic leaders in the modern world.
Explain the importance of Islamic festivals for Muslims.
'All Muslims should observe the fast during Ramadan.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 2:183-185)
n: Strong answers used the command in 2:183, then the exemptions in the same passage as the other view.

x: Identify two ways the Prophet was a role model in being a good husband.
Describe the conversation between Muhammad (pbuh) and Jibrail in the cave of Hira.
Explain the importance of mosques to the early Islamic community in Madinah.
'The most important role of the Prophet was in the establishment of the Shari'ah (deen).' Assess this statement. (Hadith on obeying rulers)
Identify two ways that the Qur'an is important to Muslims.
Describe the events of the Mi'raj.
Explain the role of the Sunnah in the establishment of Muslim belief and practice.
'The Prophethood of Muhammad (pbuh) was the only reason that Islam was successfully established.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 33:38-40)
Identify two Muslim beliefs about al-Qadr (predestination).
Describe what Muslims believe about Allah as creator.
Explain the importance of Dawud as a prophet in Islam.
'Living by correct etiquette, attitudes and manners will certainly lead Muslims to attain Jannah.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 49:11-13)
n: Strong answers used the Prophet's example and the text on not insulting others, then the five pillars as another view.

x: Identify two roles of the Risalah in Islam.
Describe what the holy book of Zabur teaches.
Explain the importance of Malaikah in Islam.
'Believing in the oneness of Allah is what makes a proper Muslim.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 112:1-4)
Identify one action that is performed when Muslims pray.
Describe the features of Eid-ul-Adha.
n: Weak answers retold the story of Ibrahim instead of describing the features of the festival.

x: Explain the importance of Laylat al-Qadr for Muslims today.
n: The best answers linked the night to Muslims' lives today, not only to the story of revelation.

x: 'Giving financial support to those in need is the most pleasing to Allah.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 9:58-60)
n: Strong answers used 9:60 and the eight groups, then argued that worship such as Salah also greatly pleases Allah.

x: Identify one purpose of marriage for Muslims.
Describe Muslim beliefs about good leadership in the community.
Explain the importance of Hajj for Muslims.
n: The best answers developed Hajj as an inner, spiritual journey rather than listing its actions.

x: 'All key Muslim beliefs are contained in the Shahadah.' Assess this statement. (Qur'an 3:18-19)
n: Strong answers showed that all beliefs flow from Tawhid and Risalah, then used the other pillars, such as Salah, as another view.
